## Proof

**Goal.** Compute $h^0\!\left(N_{C/\mathbb{P}^3}\right)$ for the twisted cubic $C\subset\mathbb{P}^3$ given by $I=(xz-y^{2},\, yw-z^{2},\, xw-yz)$, using a method that avoids the standard "split $N\cong\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(5)^{\oplus 2}$" or "Riemann–Roch + $H^{1}=0$" route.

**Method.** Restrict the Euler sequence and the normal sequence to $C$, and read off $h^{0}(N)$ from the cohomology of line bundles on $\mathbb{P}^{1}$ alone — without ever computing $\deg N$ or the splitting type.

---

### Step 1. Identify $C$ with $\mathbb{P}^{1}$

The twisted cubic is the third Veronese embedding
$$\nu_{3}:\mathbb{P}^{1}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{3},\qquad [s:t]\mapsto[s^{3}:s^{2}t:st^{2}:t^{3}],$$
whose image has exactly the ideal $I=(xz-y^{2},\,yw-z^{2},\,xw-yz)$. Hence $C\cong\mathbb{P}^{1}$, of genus $g=0$, and the hyperplane bundle restricts as
$$\mathcal{O}_{C}(1)\cong\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(3).$$

---

### Step 2. Compute $h^{0}\!\left(T_{\mathbb{P}^{3}}\big|_{C}\right)$ via the Euler sequence

Restricting the Euler sequence $0\to\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{3}}\to\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{3}}(1)^{\oplus 4}\to T_{\mathbb{P}^{3}}\to 0$ to $C$ gives
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal{O}_{C}\longrightarrow\mathcal{O}_{C}(1)^{\oplus 4}\longrightarrow T_{\mathbb{P}^{3}}\big|_{C}\longrightarrow 0.$$
Under the identification $C\cong\mathbb{P}^{1}$ this is
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}\longrightarrow\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(3)^{\oplus 4}\longrightarrow T_{\mathbb{P}^{3}}\big|_{C}\longrightarrow 0.$$

Taking global sections and using $H^{1}\!\left(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}\right)=0$ (and $H^{1}\!\left(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(3)\right)=0$), the long exact sequence yields the short exact sequence on $H^{0}$:
$$0\to H^{0}\!\left(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}\right)\to H^{0}\!\left(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(3)\right)^{\oplus 4}\to H^{0}\!\left(T_{\mathbb{P}^{3}}\big|_{C}\right)\to 0.$$
Therefore
$$h^{0}\!\left(T_{\mathbb{P}^{3}}\big|_{C}\right)=4\cdot h^{0}\!\left(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(3)\right)-h^{0}\!\left(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}\right)=4\cdot 4-1=15.$$

---

### Step 3. Use the normal sequence to extract $h^{0}(N)$

The normal sequence of the embedding $C\subset\mathbb{P}^{3}$ is
$$0\longrightarrow T_{C}\longrightarrow T_{\mathbb{P}^{3}}\big|_{C}\longrightarrow N_{C/\mathbb{P}^{3}}\longrightarrow 0.$$
Since $C\cong\mathbb{P}^{1}$, we have $T_{C}\cong\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(2)$. The long exact cohomology sequence begins
$$0\to H^{0}\!\left(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(2)\right)\to H^{0}\!\left(T_{\mathbb{P}^{3}}\big|_{C}\right)\to H^{0}\!\left(N_{C/\mathbb{P}^{3}}\right)\to H^{1}\!\left(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(2)\right)\to\cdots$$

On $\mathbb{P}^{1}$, $H^{1}\!\left(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(2)\right)=0$ (positive degree). Hence the sequence truncates to
$$0\to H^{0}\!\left(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(2)\right)\to H^{0}\!\left(T_{\mathbb{P}^{3}}\big|_{C}\right)\to H^{0}\!\left(N_{C/\mathbb{P}^{3}}\right)\to 0,$$
which gives the dimension count
$$h^{0}\!\left(N_{C/\mathbb{P}^{3}}\right)=h^{0}\!\left(T_{\mathbb{P}^{3}}\big|_{C}\right)-h^{0}\!\left(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(2)\right).$$

Now $h^{0}\!\left(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(2)\right)=2+1=3$, and from Step 2, $h^{0}\!\left(T_{\mathbb{P}^{3}}\big|_{C}\right)=15$. Therefore
$$h^{0}\!\left(N_{C/\mathbb{P}^{3}}\right)=15-3=12.$$

---

### Verification (consistency check)

As a sanity check, the same number is recovered from the splitting $N_{C/\mathbb{P}^{3}}\cong\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(5)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(5)$, which gives $h^{0}=6+6=12$, and from Riemann–Roch $\chi(N)=\deg N+2=10+2=12$ (with $H^{1}(N)=0$). All three methods agree.

---

### Conclusion

$$\boxed{h^{0}\!\left(N_{C/\mathbb{P}^{3}}\right)=12}.$$

The method above is non-standard in that it never invokes the splitting type of $N$, never computes $\deg N$ via Chern-class/degree formulas, and never applies Riemann–Roch. It obtains $h^{0}(N)$ purely from the Euler sequence restricted to $C$ and the normal sequence, reducing everything to line-bundle cohomology on $\mathbb{P}^{1}$.
